Q141119571.summary: Framed by a border of acanthus, this ivory plaque sets the crucified Christ at the centre of a crowded cosmic drama. Angels adore the cross between the sun and moon, figures personifying the Church and the Synagogue stand to either side, the lance-bearer and sponge-bearer flank the cross, and below the dead rise from their tombs while a foliate column carries the cross up from the world of Earth and Ocean. Made around the year 1000 for a precious liturgical book, it shows Ottonian carvers re-working the rich Carolingian crucifixion imagery of Metz.
facts: According to the French Wikipedia article, the plaque was commissioned by Adalbero II, Bishop of Metz (984–1005), as the cover of a precious liturgical book.
The titulus above Christ reads IHS NAZAREN REX IUDEORU ('Jesus of Nazareth, King of the Jews'), and Adam and Eve appear in contrition on the capital at the foot of the cross.
The Church (Ecclesia) is shown catching the blood from Christ's side in a vessel, while the Synagogue turns away: a pairing common in medieval crucifixion imagery.

Q141119571.notes: The Commons file is categorised under Adalbero I of Metz (bishop 929–962), but the French Wikipedia article names Adalbero II (984–1005) and dates the plaque c. 1000; this has not been checked against the museum's own catalogue. Dimensions per Wikidata: 15.4 × 9.3 cm.
